4. The leaned Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong upon hearing the parties decreed the suit on 21-7-1988 with costs and interest against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 (petitioner herein) and dismissed the same against defendant No 4. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed Execution Case before the Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong being Money Execution Case No. 14 of 1991 claiming the amount of Tk. 2,80,527 including the amount of interest @ 16%. 

 5. The suit was decreed for an amount of Tk. 80,988.48 with interest and costs. But the learned Judge did not specify in this judgment and decree dated 21-7-1988 how much and at what rate interest had to be paid to the plaintiff by defendant Nos. 1 and 2. As a result, the defendant petitioners filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to exercise inherent discretion of the Court to hold that no interest was required to be paid by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. The learned Joint District Judge 2 and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong rejected the said application under section 151 of the Code. The petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order dated 24-6-1992 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong filed Civil Revision No. 1862 of 1992 before the High Court Division. On 19-8-1997 the High Court Division by its judgment discharged the Rule and directed the Executing Court to fix up the interest at the prevailing banking rate at the time of passing the decree. The plaintiff decree-holding thereafter, filed an application before the Executing Court along with a certificate of interest rate issued by Janata Bank, EPZ Branch, Chittagong and demanded rate of interest at rate of 16%. The defendant-petitioners also filed written objection against the said application staring that Janata Bank, EPZ Branch, Chittagong was neither the Letter of Credit opening Bank nor connecting with the case in any way was and, as such, certificate of the said bank could not be acceptable. Moreso, the same certificate is not supported by any circular of Bangladesh Bank. The learned Judge of the Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong upon hearing the parties allowed the application of the decree-holder on 3-9-1998 and directed the judgment debtor to pay Tk. 4,05,237.74 as interest @ 16% on the decreetal amount from the date of filing of the suit till realization. 

 10. We have perused the Civil Revision, the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioners and other connected papers. It appears from the record that the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 field Money Suit No. 14 of 1997 in the Court of Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong for recovery of Tk. 80,98.48 against the dependent petitioners. This suit was decreed on 21-7-1988 with costs and with interest till realization of the money. But the learned Joint District Judge did not mention in the judgment the rate of interest to be paid to the plaintiff by the defendant petitioners. Therefore, the defendant-petitioners filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and prayed for allowing them to deposit the decretal amount without interest. The learned Joint District Judge rejected the application on 24-6-1992. Thereafter, the petitioner filed Civil Revision No. 1862 of 1992 before this High Court Division against the order dated 24-6-1992. The High Court Division discharged the Rule with the direction that the Executing Court should fix up the interest at the prevailing bank rate at the time of passing the decree (Annexure-C). This trial Court heard the matter on 3-9-1998 and passed the impugned order fixing the rate of interest at the rate of 16% relying on a petitioner contends that the Janata Bank is in no way connected with this suit. So the Janata Bank had no competence to submit any paper showing the prevailing rate of interest. Though the Janata Bank filed the papers showing that the relevant time the prevailing cute of interest was 18% the plaintiff claimed 16% interest and the Court allowed 16% interest in favour of the plaintiff. The petitioners by filing a supplementary affidavit annexed some papers from Bangladesh Bank showing that at the relevant time of passing the decree the prevailing rate of interest was 10.75% (Annexure-D and D(1)). Therefore, we are getting two types of Bank rate at the relevant time of passing the decree. In fact the certificate given by Janata Bank is not before us. Therefore, it is not possible for us to ascertain the basis of the certificate given by the Janata Bank about the prevailing rate of interest. The petitioners by filing supplementary affidavit submitted Annexure-D and D (1) showing that the prevailing rate of interest at the relevant time of passing the decree was 10.75%. It is difficult for us to ascertain whether the certificate given by Janata Bank is correct or the certificate given by the Bangladesh Bank is genuine. In such a situation, we find that it would be proper to direct the lower Court to ascertain which certificate is genuine and correct, whether the certificate given by the Janata Bank or the papers submitted by the petitioners in then supplementary affidavit. 

 11. Considering all these aspects of the case, we are of the opinion that this is a fit case to send the record back on remained to the lower Court for ascertaining the prevailing rate of interest at the time of passing the decree. 

 12. Considering the facts and circumstances and the reasons mentioned hereinbefore, the case is sent back on remand to the lower Court to ascertain the prevailing bank rate at the relevant time of passing the decree. 

 13. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the case is sent back on remand to the Court of Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong. The impugned judgment and order dated 3-9-1998 passed by the learned Joint District Judge and judge of the Commercial Court, No. 2 Chittagong is hereby set-aside. The learned Joint District Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Chittagong is directed to ascertain the decree and fix up the rate of interest to be paid to the plaintiff along with the decreetal amount and dispose of the money suit accordingly an expeditiously as possible.
